explanations: terra: Israel is told to remember the نعمة Allah bestowed and fulfill the covenant. It identifies the same favored people whose provision later meets the warning of wrath.
terra: Allah recalls the نعمة bestowed on Israel and their special favor over peoples. It gives the phrase of bestowed favor a collective historical addressee.
terra: In the calf narrative, Moses calls his people to repentance, and Allah accepts it. This supplies a repentance route out of the calf episode whose wrath is explicit in 7:152.

luna: In the wilderness, God shades Israel with cloud and sends manna and quail, then tells them to eat from the good provision; this is another direct provision scene behind 20:81's gift-and-warning pattern. | terra: Cloud shade, manna, quail, and the command to eat good provision repeat the provision scene quoted by the section before 20:81's warning.

terra: Israel is told to enter, eat abundantly, enter the gate prostrating, and ask for remission; forgiveness and increase await the doers of good. It binds plentiful favor, a bowed face, and pardon.

luna: After the command to enter and ask forgiveness in 2:58, the wrongdoers are struck by punishment from heaven; the verse gives the descent that follows refusal of a given way. | terra: The wrongdoers alter the commanded word, so a punishment is sent down upon them from heaven. It reverses 2:58's gift and remission with a descending consequence.
terra: After water is given from the rock, Israel is told to eat and drink Allah's provision and not spread corruption. It is another gift with a boundary against misuse.

luna: Israel asks for other food after the manna, and the verse says humiliation was laid upon them and they incurred anger from God (بَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ); it closely joins rejected provision, abasement, and anger. | terra: After rejecting the given food for lesser substitutes, Israel receives abasement and returns with غضب upon غضب. It makes misuse of provision lead to the section's falling wrath and lowliness.

luna: The verse says they incurred anger upon anger (بَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ عَلَىٰ غَضَبٍ) for rejecting what God revealed; it is a repeated formulation of anger settling on a group. | terra: Those who reject Allah's revelation out of envy return with غضب upon غضب. The repeated burdened return sharpens the section's language of wrath as an acquired descent.
terra: The repeated reminder of Allah's نعمة to Israel keeps the gift before the community that later chooses the calf and receives warnings of غضب.
terra: Allah sees the Prophet turn his face toward heaven and gives him a qibla that will please him. It directly joins face-direction and rıza before 2:150 completes favor and guidance.
terra: The command repeatedly turns faces toward the Sacred Mosque so that Allah may complete His favor and guide the community. It joins face, نعمة, and guidance in one direction.

luna: A person gives himself seeking God's pleasure (ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ); this is a specific path of seeking the acceptance that the section contrasts with anger. | terra: A person gives himself seeking Allah's pleasure (مَرْضَات). It makes rıza a concrete motive for self-offering rather than a detached reward.
terra: Spending seeks Allah's pleasure and is pictured through a fruitful garden. It gives the pursuit of rıza an enacted, nourishing form.

luna: The verse places gardens and God's approval among the promised good for the mindful; it joins bestowed reward to the رضا pole the section sets against anger. | terra: For the God-fearing, gardens and Allah's رضوان are presented as better than worldly desire. It places rıza among the enduring favorable gifts.
terra: Allah's favor turns enemies into brothers by joining their hearts and rescues them from a pit of Fire. Its inner softening and rescue extend the favorable side of the image.

luna: At judgment some faces whiten and others blacken (تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ); this is a direct alternative account of judgment appearing in two faces. | terra: On the Day, faces are whitened and blackened, and the blackened faces are confronted with their disbelief. It makes the final division visible on the face.

luna: The whitened faces are in God's mercy; the verse identifies the favorable meaning of the facial sign introduced in 3:106. | terra: The whitened faces are in Allah's mercy forever. It supplies the mercy-side outcome of the facial division in 3:106.

luna: Humiliation is laid upon a people and they incur anger from God for disbelief and rebellion; this repeats the section's combination of an imposed mark and divine anger. | terra: Humiliation is struck upon them and they return with غضب from Allah. The verse visually couples wrath with the lowly condition that the section finds in the adverse face.

luna: Those hostile to believers bite their fingertips from rage (الْغَيْظِ); this is a visible bodily gesture of anger, a parallel to the section's dictionary claim that anger shows itself in the body. | terra: Hostile people bite their fingertips in rage when alone. It is an indirect bodily overflow of anger beside the section's facial and eye signs.
luna: The call to race toward forgiveness and a Garden prepared for the mindful gives a direct path toward the accepted outcome.

luna: The righteous restrain rage and pardon people; the verse gives an ethical opposite to the bodily eruption in the section's B001 gloss for anger, using the related but different word الغيظ. | terra: The God-fearing restrain anger and pardon people, and Allah loves the doers of good. It gives a human reversal of anger's urge toward retaliation.
luna: Those who remember their wrong and seek forgiveness are described as not persisting knowingly; the verse gives repentance as a route away from anger's adverse end.

luna: Their reward is forgiveness and Gardens; this closes the sequence with the favorable end after the anger-restraint and repentance in 3:134–135, and uses ni'ma as an approving formula for the reward. | terra: Forgiveness and gardens are followed by "excellent is the reward of the workers" (نِعْمَ). The praise-word sense of the section's نعمة marks the favorable verdict.
luna: By God's mercy, the Prophet is gentle with his companions and is told to pardon and seek forgiveness for them; it gives a concrete soft-and-forgiving stance opposite harshness.

luna: The verse contrasts following God's pleasure (رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ) with returning with His displeasure (بِسَخَطٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ); the section's lexicon explicitly calls anger the opposite of riḍā. | terra: It sets following Allah's رضوان against returning burdened with His سخط, the section's central rıza/gazap fork cast as two opposed destinations.
terra: Allah confers favor on believers by sending a messenger who recites, purifies, and teaches. It explains one way divine favor becomes guidance.
luna: Believers answer a threat by saying God is sufficient for them and an excellent trustee (نِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ); this is another explicit instance of the section's secondary ni'ma-as-praise sense.
terra: Believers return with Allah's favor and bounty, unharmed, having followed His رضوان. It is a positive return set against returning with غضب.
terra: A warning threatens to efface faces and turn them backward, or to curse as earlier transgressors were cursed. Facial reversal is joined to the wrath-adjacent curse category.

luna: The verse calls God's command to return trusts and judge justly a good instruction (نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِ); this is the section's secondary dictionary sense of ni'ma as a word of commendation, not a granted favor.

luna: This verse promises guidance to a straight path immediately before 4:69 names the people God has favored; it makes the “way” of the favored companions explicit. | terra: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger would guide them to a straight path. It is the immediate path-condition before 4:69's company of those favored.

luna: The verse names those God favored—prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and the righteous—and ends by calling them good companions; it directly supports the section's reading of the favored path as a shared walk. | terra: It names the people whom Allah has favored (أَنْعَمَ) and calls prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people beautiful companions, exactly developing the section's shared road.
terra: After the companions of those favored in 4:69, the ayah calls that company Allah's فضل. It identifies their companionship as a divine gift.
terra: Deliberate murder brings Allah's غضب, curse, and Hell. It gives the wrath category an explicit judgmental consequence rather than a passing human emotion.
terra: Private counsel for charity, right, or reconciliation is commended when it seeks Allah's pleasure. The verse gives rıza a socially reparative course.
terra: Allah asks why He would punish if people are grateful and believe. It places gratitude on the side opposed to the punitive outcome underlying the section's wrath.
terra: Allah completes His نعمة and says He has approved Islam as religion. It joins the section's active bestowal of favor to explicit divine rıza.
terra: Purification is followed by Allah's wish to complete His favor so that people may be grateful. It links cleansing, نعمة, and gratitude without the adverse fall.
terra: Covenant-breaking brings Allah's curse and hardens hearts. It gives a moral and inward counterpart to the wrath-side's adverse marking.
terra: Allah guides those who follow His رضوان to paths of peace and ultimately a straight path. It makes the favorable side of 1:7 a route, not merely a verdict.
terra: Moses tells Israel to remember Allah's favor in making prophets and kings among them. It supplies the older gift-history behind the calf and provision narratives.

luna: The verse names people God has cursed and become angry with (غَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ), then says they are farther from the even way; it joins anger to the lost-path side of the image. | terra: Allah's curse and غضب are joined to being farther astray from the level path. It directly confirms the section's meeting of wrath with losing the way.

luna: The verse says God's anger is upon people who take disbelievers as allies and that they will abide in punishment; it connects anger to conduct and lasting outcome. | terra: Their alliances are called an evil advance because Allah is displeased with them and they remain in punishment. سخط supplies the section's close antonymic field for غضب.
terra: On hearing revelation, their eyes overflow with tears because they recognize truth. This is an indirect but specific eye-response parallel to 19:58's prostration and weeping.
terra: Believers are told not to forbid the good things Allah made lawful and not to transgress. It repeats 20:81's provision joined to a boundary against excess.
terra: The next ayah commands eating the lawful, good provision Allah gives. Its own contribution is the gift whose misuse 5:87 forbids.

luna: On “this day,” God says He is pleased with the truthful and they with Him (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ); the verse makes the section's two-way رضا explicit at judgment. | terra: On the Day when truthfulness benefits the truthful, Allah says He is pleased with them and they with Him. It joins the section's yawm of judgment to its favorable face.
terra: After the wrongdoing people are cut off, the declaration is "praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds." It places حمد beside a completed punitive day without making praise into blame.

luna: The people of the Garden praise God for guiding them there (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدَانَا); it ties the section's hamd/approval word to the guided, favored path. | terra: Garden-dwellers say praise belongs to Allah who guided them; they confess they could not have been guided without Him. Their hamd is the speech of the favored, guided side.
terra: Hud tells his people that defilement and غضب from their Lord have already fallen upon them; it repeats the section's spatial image of wrath landing on a people.
luna: Thamud kill the she-camel and defy their Lord's command, then demand that punishment be brought; their chosen defiance reverses the section's picture of receiving a gift and following guidance.
luna: The earthquake seizes the defiant Thamud immediately after 7:77; the verse gives the punishment that descends after their refusal.
luna: God says that belief and mindfulness would have opened blessings from heaven and earth, but denial led to seizure; it directly links response to favor with the opposite outcome.

luna: After recognizing that they had gone astray over the calf, the people fear loss unless God shows mercy; the verse links lost direction with the possibility of mercy in the same episode as 7:150–153. | terra: After taking the calf, they recognize that they have gone astray and appeal for mercy and forgiveness. It makes misguidance and hoped-for pardon explicit within the wrath narrative.

luna: Musa returns to his people angry and sorrowful, just as 20:86 does; the episode gives the section's bodily and spoken form of anger in a second account. | terra: Moses returns to his people غضبان أسفا. It is the parallel bodily scene to 20:86 for the section's dictionary sense of anger visible in a person.

luna: Musa asks God to forgive him and his brother and admit them into mercy; this is the pardon side of the calf episode's anger-and-humiliation outcome. | terra: Moses asks forgiveness for himself and Aaron and asks to be admitted into mercy. The plea follows his angry return and opens the mercy side of the episode.

luna: The calf-makers are promised anger from their Lord and humiliation (غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌ); the verse directly stages anger reaching a group and a bodily/social abasement. | terra: Those who took the calf are promised غضب from their Lord and humiliation. The paired burden makes the section's wrath-and-lowliness reading concrete.

luna: Those who do wrong and then repent and believe find their Lord forgiving and merciful; this continuation sets return and pardon against the prior calf judgment. | terra: After the calf episode, those who repent and believe find their Lord forgiving and merciful. It gives a return from the wrath-and-humiliation warning of 7:152.

luna: After Musa's anger subsides, he takes the tablets, whose inscription contains guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord; this joins the anger scene to the guided, forgiven path. | terra: When Moses' anger subsides, the tablets yield guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord. Its cooling of anger leads into the guided side of the contrast.
luna: After an earthquake seizes the appointed group, Musa asks God to forgive them and show mercy; this continues the section's anger, punishment, and pardon themes in the same narrative.
luna: Musa asks for good in this life and the next, and God says His mercy encompasses all things; the verse extends the plea for mercy into a stated divine gift.
luna: The successful are those who follow the Messenger and the light sent down with him; this makes following guidance the route into the mercy described in 7:156.

luna: This parallel wilderness account again names cloud, manna, quail, and provision from God; it makes the gift that precedes the warning in the section concrete. | terra: The cloud, manna, quail, and good provision recur for Israel; their self-wronging supplies the moral pressure behind the section's warning against transgression in a gift.

luna: Israel is told to enter the town, eat freely, and enter the gate prostrating while asking forgiveness; the verse places a path of submission and pardon beside the provision scene. | terra: The parallel command grants plentiful food, requires entry prostrating, and promises forgiveness and increase. It repeats the section's gift, face-to-ground, and mercy pattern.

luna: After the people alter the command in 7:161, punishment is sent down on the wrongdoers; the reversal makes the gift, instruction, and adverse outcome a connected sequence. | terra: Those who wrong the command receive a punishment sent down from heaven. Its descent is the adverse counterpart to the granted abundance in 7:161.
terra: One who turns away in battle, except for tactical reasons, returns with غضب from Allah and has Hell as destination. The verb of return makes wrath the opposite end of a path.
terra: At death the angels strike the faces and backs of those who disbelieve and announce the burning punishment. It is a direct bodily mark of the adverse verdict.
terra: The Lord announces mercy, His رضوان, and gardens to the believers who migrate and strive. It joins rıza to a promised communal destination.
terra: Some are pleased when given charity and become angry when not given it. The verse makes receiving a gift visibly divide rıza from its opposite, in a human and morally exposed form.
terra: It tells the dissatisfied to be content with what Allah and His Messenger gave and to await further فضل. It clarifies the proper response to the gift in 9:58.

luna: The verse names God's pleasure as greater than the gardens promised to believers; it clarifies that favor culminates in acceptance, not material provision alone. | terra: After gardens, rivers, and good dwellings, the ayah says Allah's رضوان is greater. It treats rıza as the crowning favorable gift.
terra: People may seek the believers' pleasure, but Allah does not approve the defiantly disobedient. The boundary distinguishes human appeasement from the rıza that matters in the section.

luna: God is pleased with the first believers and they are pleased with Him, with gardens prepared for them; this closely identifies a community of favor through reciprocal acceptance. | terra: The first Emigrants, Helpers, and those who follow them well receive Allah's rıza and the Garden; the verse supplies another defined company on the favored course.

luna: One foundation seeks God's pleasure (رِضْوَانٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ), while the other is on a crumbling bank that collapses with its builder into Hell; this links pleasure with a steady course and its opposite with falling.

luna: The people of the Garden's final utterance is praise to God; this gives hamd as the response of those who have reached the favorable end. | terra: The final call of Garden-dwellers is praise to Allah. It places حمد at the settled end of the favorable path.

luna: Those who do good receive the best and more, and neither dust nor abasement covers their faces (قَتَرٌ وَلَا ذِلَّةٌ); the verse makes the unmarked face a sign of the favorable outcome. | terra: Those who do good receive the best and more; neither dust-darkness nor humiliation covers their faces. It directly negates the covering scene of 80:40–41.

luna: Those who earn evil have faces as if covered by pieces of dark night; the verse supplies the opposite facial outcome to 10:26 and to the section's softened face. | terra: Those who earn evil have faces covered as by pieces of dark night and are humiliated. It is the adverse face that 10:26 excludes for the good-doers.
terra: When Allah's command came, Hud and believers with him were saved by mercy from a harsh punishment. It supplies the pardon-and-rescue side of the 'Ad days named in the section.
terra: When Allah's command came, Salih and believers were saved by mercy from that day's humiliation. It gives Thamud the same day, mercy, and abasement pattern.
terra: The blast seizes the wrongdoers of Thamud and leaves them lifeless in their homes. It supplies the punitive side completed by the mercy-and-day rescue of 11:66.
terra: Yusuf is chosen, taught, and promised the completion of his Lord's favor upon him and Jacob's family. It shows نعمة arriving as election and understanding.

luna: Jacob's eyes whiten from grief (وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ); this is a distinct eye-state from the section's anger-swelling and coolness, but specifically shows emotion registered in the eyes. | terra: Jacob's eyes turn white from grief. Unlike the section's anger-swollen eye, it is an indirect contrary case showing inner suffering visibly altering the eye.
terra: When Yusuf's shirt is placed over Jacob's face, Jacob's sight returns. This reverses the grief-altered eyes of 12:84, though its emotion is reunion rather than anger.
terra: The revealed Book brings people from darkness into light and guides them to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy (الحميد). It gives the section's حمد a path-form.

luna: This is the section's quoted command: Musa must remind his people of “the days of Allah” (أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ), the exact yawm wording whose gloss includes punishment and pardon. | terra: Moses is ordered to remind his people of the أيام الله. It is the source wording for the section's days that carry both punishment and favor.

luna: Musa's next words specify the remembrance commanded in 14:5: God saved Israel from Pharaoh's people, naming deliverance as a favor within these “days.” | terra: Moses immediately makes the Days of Allah concrete by recalling deliverance from Pharaoh. It gives 14:5 a saved people before the later warning and gratitude test.

luna: The following verse makes gratitude lead to increase and ingratitude meet severe punishment; it connects bestowed favor with the opposite outcome that structures the section. | terra: Gratitude brings increase while ingratitude meets severe punishment. It makes the section's gift-versus-adverse-descent division a response to نعمة.
terra: After the gratitude-and-punishment division of 14:7, Moses calls Allah rich and praiseworthy. It distinguishes Allah's حمد from human gratitude or ingratitude.
luna: The verse says people exchanged God's favor (نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ) for disbelief and brought their people to ruin; it directly stages bestowed favor reversed into an adverse end.
luna: The next verse names Hell as the destination of those who brought their people to ruin; it completes the consequence begun in 14:28.
luna: They set up rivals to lead people away from God's path; this connects the rejection of favor in 14:28 with the section's lost-way group.

luna: Abraham praises God for granting him Ishmael and Isaac in old age; this is a specific instance of hamd answering bestowed favor, the link named in the section. | terra: Abraham praises Allah for granting Ishmael and Isaac in old age. It makes حمد the verbal reception of a particular bestowed gift.
terra: The arrogant are told to enter Hell, and its dwelling is called بِئْس. It supplies the blame-word that the section explicitly sets opposite the praise-form نِعْمَ.
terra: The God-fearing call what their Lord sent "good," and the Hereafter's home is described with the praise form نِعْمَ. It realizes the section's dictionary sense of ni'ma as commendation.
terra: Gardens of lasting residence complete the "excellent home of the God-fearing" in 16:30. The ayah gives that praise-word its favorable destination.
terra: Every favor possessed is from Allah, and harm makes people call on Him. It states the gift-and-distress alternation underneath the section's two conditions.

luna: When one of them hears news of a daughter, his face darkens (مُسْوَدًّا); this is a different cause from divine anger, but specifically makes the face disclose an inward reaction as in the section's image. | terra: At the birth-news he dislikes, a man's face darkens while he is constricted. It is a human-scale parallel to the section's angry, visibly altered face.
luna: The man hides from people in shame after his face darkens in 16:58; this clarifies the social and inward force of that visible facial sign.
terra: They recognize Allah's favor and then deny it. The verse identifies refusal to acknowledge نعمة as a concrete turn away from the favorable response.
terra: After faith, a deliberately opened breast to disbelief incurs Allah's غضب and a great punishment. It defines a moral turning that reaches the anger side of the section.

luna: The secure town had provision from every direction, then denied God's favors and was made to taste hunger and fear; it is a precise provision-to-reversal scene. | terra: A secure, richly provided town denies Allah's favors, then tastes a garment of hunger and fear. The verse reverses نعمة into an enclosing bodily affliction.
luna: A messenger came to that town and its people denied him, so punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers; this completes the preceding reversal.
terra: Eat what Allah has provided, lawful and good, and be grateful for His نعمة. It restates the provision-and-restraint ethic of 20:81 without the transgression.
terra: Abraham is grateful for Allah's favors; Allah chooses him and guides him to a straight path. The verse directly fuses ni'ma, gratitude, election, and the road of 1:6–7.
terra: The punitive incursion is sent to disfigure faces and enter the sanctuary. It makes the section's claim that judgment leaves a facial trace concrete in history.
luna: The one who seeks the Hereafter, strives for it, and believes has a recognized effort; this parallels the section's satisfied effort in 88:9, though it does not use رضا.
terra: Whoever is blind in this life is blind in the Hereafter and farther astray from the way. It connects the section's eye imagery to its lost-path side.
terra: When Allah bestows favor, the human turns away; when evil touches him, he despairs. This is a direct reversal of the grateful, calm reception of نعمة.
terra: The one Allah leaves astray is gathered on the Day upon his face, blind, mute, and deaf, with Hell as destination. It joins guidance versus straying to an overturned, sightless face.
terra: Those given knowledge fall on their chins in prostration when the Quran is recited. It repeats 19:58's favored response as a bodily lowering of the face.
terra: They fall on their chins weeping and it increases them in humility. This is the same prostration-and-tears scene the section attaches to those granted guidance.

luna: The warning to disbelievers describes water that scalds faces and calls it an evil drink (بِئْسَ الشَّرَابُ); this joins the section's face-mark image to its dictionary contrast between commendation and blame. | terra: The warning that scalding water sears faces is a plausible extension of the section's face under adverse judgment, though its own image is infernal heat rather than غضب or facial emotion.
luna: The next verse promises that believers who do good will not lose their reward; it supplies the other side of the choice introduced in 18:29.
luna: The believers receive the Garden, and the verse calls their reward excellent (نِعْمَ الثَّوَابُ); alongside 18:29's bi'sa, it directly realizes the section's secondary ni'ma/bi'sa contrast.

luna: Mary is told to eat, drink, and be comforted (وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا); this is another exact Qur'anic use of eye-coolness for relief and gift. | terra: Mary is told to eat, drink, and cool her eye. Provision and an eye made calm appear together, just as the section places ni'ma in the softened face.

luna: Those God favored, guided, and chose fall down prostrating and weeping; this is the section's exact link between bestowed favor, guidance, and a visible bodily response. | terra: The people Allah favored are also those guided and chosen; upon hearing the signs they fall prostrate and weeping. It joins favor, guidance, and the section's face-to-ground response.
terra: After 19:58's favored people who fall prostrate, later successors neglect prayer, follow desire, and meet misguidance. It is the immediate contrary line of descent.
terra: Those who repent, believe, and act righteously enter the Garden without injustice. It gives the recovery from 19:59's misguidance its own promised destination.
terra: Allah tells Moses that He had bestowed favor on him before. It anchors Moses' later haste for divine pleasure and anger over the calf in a prior favor.

luna: Musa's mother is promised that her eye will be cooled and she will not grieve (تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا); this is the Qur'anic bodily expression behind the section's dictionary gloss for the eye's blessing. | terra: Allah returns Moses to his mother so that her eye may be cooled and she will not grieve. This is the section's exact Quranic counterpart to the eye's نعمة as settled coolness.

luna: God tells Musa and Harun to speak gently to Pharaoh (قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا); this is the softness side of the section's dictionary contrast, using a different root, and addresses the same speakers as its anger narrative.

luna: This is the rescue-and-provision scene immediately before 20:81: Israel is saved from its enemy and given manna and quail, so the warning about transgression follows a concrete gift. | terra: Before 20:81, Allah recalls saving Israel from its enemy and sending down manna and quail. This ayah supplies the rescue and provision that make the subsequent wrath warning sharp.

luna: The verse joins provision (رَزَقْنَاكُمْ) to the command not to transgress and the warning “My anger may come upon you” (فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي); it makes the two descents in the section a single conditional scene. | terra: The section's quoted manna-and-quail scene makes provision and restraint precede the warning that Allah's غضب may يَحِلّ "upon" its recipients; it is the clearest realization of the descending thing in 1:7.

luna: After the fall named in 20:81, God promises abundant forgiveness to the one who repents, believes, acts well, and is guided (ثُمَّ اهْتَدَىٰ); this is the passage's stated path out of the warning. | terra: Immediately after the fall under wrath in 20:81, forgiveness is promised to the repentant, faithful, righteous person who is then guided; it supplies the other end of the section's fall-versus-guidance contrast.
terra: Moses says he hastened to his Lord "so that You may be pleased" (لِتَرْضَى); his movement toward rıza frames the calf episode and his angry return in the following passage.

luna: God tells Musa that He has tested his people and that Samiri led them astray; this identifies the lost-way cause immediately before Musa returns angry in 20:86. | terra: Allah says the people were tested after Moses and that the Samiri led them astray. It supplies the causal straying behind Moses' angry return in 20:86.

luna: Musa returns to his people “angry and grieving” (غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا) after the calf episode, then asks if they wanted their Lord's anger to come upon them; anger is both bodily stance and threatened descent here. | terra: This one ayah joins Moses' return غضبان أسفا with his question whether the people wanted wrath from their Lord to descend upon them, directly joining the angry face and the falling verdict.
terra: Faces humble themselves before the Living, the Sustainer, while the bearer of wrongdoing fails. It gives the Day's judgment a visible, lowered face.
terra: When guidance comes, whoever follows it will neither go astray nor be wretched. It gives the guided alternative to the fall under wrath in the same surah.
terra: The one who turns from the reminder has a constricted life and is gathered blind on the Day. It gives straying a particular adverse eye-state.
terra: The command to glorify with the Lord's حمد is paired with "perhaps you will be pleased." It binds the section's hamd and rıza in the same address.

terra: The addressee is told not to extend his eyes toward temporary worldly splendor; the Lord's provision is better and more lasting. It develops the eye and provision immediately after the praise-to-satisfaction command in 20:130.
terra: The unbelievers will be unable to keep Fire from their faces or backs. The face becomes the exposed surface of the adverse judgment.
luna: On the Day of Resurrection, just scales are set up and no soul is wronged; this gives a concrete judgment-day scene for the section's yawm and two-outcome frame.
terra: When the true promise nears, disbelievers' eyes stare fixedly. This only indirectly relates to the section's eye imagery, but it is a specific eschatological eye-state.
terra: Many beings prostrate to Allah, while many people deserve punishment and are humiliated by Him. It sets prostration beside the adverse judgment that cannot be honored away.
terra: Those who are guided receive good speech and are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy (الحميد). It directly reunites the section's حمد with the straight-path image.
terra: Those driven out for Allah's cause are admitted to an entrance they will be pleased with. It supplies a concrete, favorable entry for the language of rıza.
luna: The verse calls God an excellent protector and helper (نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ); this uses the section's commendatory ni'ma form for the one who gives protection.
terra: Noah is told to say praise to Allah who saved them from wrongdoing people. It makes deliverance from an adverse collective into a reason for حمد.

luna: The Fire scorches the faces of its people (تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ), who grimace; this is a direct bodily reversal of the cool, softened face in the section. | terra: Fire scorches their faces and leaves them grimacing. This is the bodily extreme of the section's adverse face under divine judgment.
terra: Allah's favor and mercy are said to be what makes purification possible. It gives the favorable side an inward cleansing rather than a facial sign.

luna: The servants ask for spouses and children as “comfort to our eyes” (قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ), tying the section's eye-coolness sense to a prayer for a blessed household and righteous leadership. | terra: The servants ask for spouses and descendants to be قرة أعين. It extends the section's eye-coolness from a private rescue to a hoped-for household gift.
terra: David and Solomon receive knowledge and answer with praise to Allah. This gives the section's hamd a grateful response to a recognizable favor.
terra: Solomon asks to be grateful for the نعمة bestowed on him and his parents and to do a righteous deed Allah approves. Gratitude turns favor toward rıza.
terra: Those who arrive with evil are thrown face-first into the Fire. It turns the adverse course into a literal downward facial posture.

luna: In the same infant-Musa story, Pharaoh's wife calls him a comfort to her eyes (قُرَّتَ عَيْنٍ); it is another exact use of the eye-coolness sense named in the section. | terra: Pharaoh's wife calls the rescued infant a قرة عين, a coolness of the eye. The scene gives the section's calm eye image a concrete gift and rescue.

luna: Musa is returned to his mother so her eye may be cooled and she not grieve; it repeats the eye-coolness phrase in the same rescue story as 20:40. | terra: Moses is returned to his mother so that her eye may be cooled, her grief cease, and she know Allah's promise true. Favor here visibly repairs the eye's sorrow.
terra: Allah has praise in the first and last life, and judgment belongs to Him. It brings حمد into the same final judgment horizon as the section's yawm.

luna: Those who believe and do good are promised high chambers and the verse calls this an excellent reward (فَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ); this is the section's secondary ni'ma-as-commendation form applied to a favorable end. | terra: Believers who act righteously are lodged in Garden chambers, and their reward is called نِعْمَ. The praise-form of the section's ni'ma judges their work favorably.
terra: When reminded of the signs, believers fall prostrate, glorify with their Lord's حمد, and avoid arrogance. It joins the section's praise and face-to-ground response.

luna: No soul knows what eye-comfort is hidden for the righteous as reward; this directly develops the section's eye-coolness gloss as an unseen good awaiting the favored. | terra: A hidden reward is described as قرة أعين. The section's cool, quiet eye becomes a promised form of favor beyond present sight.
terra: The faithful receive gardens as lodging for their deeds, while the defiantly disobedient have Fire as lodging. It mirrors the section's two end-groups without relying on the same root.
terra: The man is described as one on whom Allah bestowed favor and on whom the Messenger bestowed favor. Its active grammar supplies a clear agent for an'amta-type benefaction.
terra: The ayah explicitly joins cooled eyes, absence of grief, and being pleased with what is given. It realizes the section's dictionary sense of the eye's نعمة as calmness alongside rıza.
terra: Those given knowledge see the revelation as truth that guides to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy. It repeats the specific hamd-and-path meeting of 14:1 and 22:24.
luna: Sheba is given a good land and told to eat from its Lord's provision and be grateful; this is a concrete gift-before-response scene like 20:80–81.
luna: After Sheba turns away, a flood is sent and their gardens are replaced; the verse makes rejection of provision issue in a loss that contrasts with the granted good land.
luna: The text identifies the punishment as recompense for their ingratitude; this completes the favor-to-punishment relation in 34:15–16.
terra: A Garden-dweller says that without his Lord's نعمة he would have been among those brought to punishment. Favor is what separates him from the adverse company.
terra: Allah gives Solomon to David and calls him an excellent servant (نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ). Bestowal and approval meet in the dictionary sense of ni'ma developed by the section.
terra: After Job's trial, Allah calls him an excellent servant (نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ). This applies the section's dictionary praise-form to a patient servant restored under divine judgment.
terra: Allah does not approve disbelief but approves gratitude. This gives the section's hamd/ni'ma side an ethical opposite to divine displeasure.

luna: The believers' skins and hearts soften at God's reminder (تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ); this is a bodily softening parallel to the section's B002 gloss for ن ع م, though the verse uses a different root. | terra: At remembrance, skins that shiver become soft and hearts soften. This directly extends the section's dictionary image of a thing becoming soft and tender on the favorable side.
terra: The one who tries to shield himself from the evil punishment with his face has no protected side left. It is a stark reversal of the face receiving favorable radiance.
luna: The call not to despair of God's mercy because He forgives sins gives the pardon side of the section's two outcomes.
luna: People are told to turn to their Lord and submit before punishment comes; the verse connects repentance with avoiding the descent of the other outcome.
luna: The command to follow the best of what was sent down before punishment arrives gives a concrete guided path, rather than mere shared religious vocabulary.
luna: The warned person imagines regretting neglect of God's side; this is the first stated consequence of failing to respond to guidance before judgment.
luna: The regret continues as the person admits that, had God guided them, they would have been among the mindful; it directly joins missed guidance to the rejected path.
luna: The person imagines another chance to do good and join the righteous; it clarifies what was refused before the judgment scene.
luna: God's answer recalls that signs came but were denied and the person was arrogant; it states the choice behind the adverse outcome.

luna: On the Resurrection Day, those who lied about God have blackened faces; this is an exact parallel to the section's face as the mark of an outcome. | terra: On resurrection day, liars' faces are blackened. It supplies an explicit dark facial sign for the unfavorable verdict.
luna: God saves the God-fearing to their place of attainment, with no evil touching them; this provides the other outcome beside the blackened faces in 39:60.
luna: Disbelievers are driven in groups to Hell and its gates open; this explicitly stages one of two gathered communities at judgment.
luna: The keepers ask whether messengers came with signs and the people confess; this identifies why the group in 39:71 receives that end.
luna: The God-fearing are led in groups to the Garden, whose gates open for them; the parallel scene gives the favorable gathering opposite 39:71.

luna: The Garden's people praise God for fulfilling His promise and giving them the land; the verse joins hamd to bestowed reward and the completed path. | terra: Those entering the Garden praise Allah for fulfilling His promise and giving them the land. Their حمد belongs to the completed favorable destination.
terra: At the final judgment angels praise their Lord and judgment is made in truth before the praise declaration. It connects the section's hamd to its Day-of-judgment horizon.

luna: The condemned are told to enter Hell and are told it is an evil abode (فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ); this supplies the bi'sa pole paired with the section's dictionary gloss of ni'ma as praise opposite blame.

luna: Aad are struck by a furious wind during days of misfortune and taste humiliating punishment; this directly recalls the section's gloss of God's days as punishment coming upon Aad. | terra: A violent wind is sent upon 'Ad in days of misfortune so they taste humiliating punishment. It realizes the section's dictionary explanation of Allah's days as descending punishment on 'Ad.

luna: Angels descend upon those who say their Lord is God and remain steadfast (تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ), telling them not to fear or grieve; this is a close positive counterpart to anger descending upon a group.
luna: The descending angels say they are the believers' allies in this life and the next, and announce the Garden; this specifies the favor of the descent in 41:30.
luna: The angels promise forgiveness and noble provision; this completes the favorable message in 41:30–31.
terra: Those who dispute Allah after response has come have void proof, wrath upon them, and severe punishment. It is another collective under the named غضب verdict.

luna: This verse says that when believers become angry (غَضِبُوا), they forgive; it presents a human response that interrupts anger, rather than the divine anger that descends in the section. | terra: Believers avoid grave sins and, when angry, forgive. Its anger-to-forgiveness movement illuminates the section's contrary endings of wrath and pardon.
terra: Those exposed to Fire are humbled by humiliation and look with a furtive eye. The ayah shows abasement as an eye-and-face posture.

luna: When one is given the news he attributes to the Merciful, his face darkens and he suppresses anger; this is a distinct human scene where the face carries a reaction, rather than the section's divine judgment scene. | terra: The same darkened, constricted face appears when one is given news of what he ascribes to the Merciful. It reiterates anger or shame taking a facial form.
luna: In the Garden are what souls desire and what delights the eyes (تَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ); this is a close semantic parallel to the section's cooled, content eye.

luna: The verse tells believers to forgive those who do not expect God's days, because He will recompense each people for what they earned; it directly uses “God's days” for the reckoning theme in the section. | terra: Those who do not expect the أيام الله are set beside the coming recompense for what each people earned. It makes the section's "days" a horizon of judgment as well as remembered events.
terra: After the preceding scene of every community judged, all praise is assigned to Allah. It makes حمد the verbal seal of a differentiated Day.
terra: The human who recognizes parental burden asks to be grateful for Allah's favor and to act in a way He approves. It repeats the section's favor-to-rıza relation in a lived appeal.
terra: Allah's curse makes them deaf and blinds their eyes. It gives the cursed, wrath-adjacent side a direct impairment of the eye.
terra: When angels take the disbelievers, they strike their faces and backs. It gives divine rejection a direct injury to the face.

luna: The condemned followed what angered God and disliked His pleasure (أَسْخَطَ اللَّهَ ... وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوَانَهُ); this directly joins the section's anger/pleasure opposition to a chosen course. | terra: They follow what angers Allah and hate His رضوان. This is the section's rıza/gazap opposition stated as two rival courses of action.
terra: Forgiveness, the completion of Allah's نعمة, and guidance to a straight path occur together. It gives the favored course the same direction the section finds after wrath's fall.

luna: God's anger is stated against hypocrites and idolaters, with Hell prepared for them; this is a distinct group judgment matching the section's anger-and-destination side. | terra: Hypocritical men and women who expect evil of Allah receive the evil turn, curse, and His غضب. The verse locates wrath within a self-confirming hostile stance.

luna: After the pledge at the tree, God is pleased with the believers and sends tranquility down upon them; the verse joins رضا to an embodied, descending gift. | terra: Allah is pleased with the believers at the pledge, knows what is in their hearts, and sends tranquility. It shows rıza arriving with an inward, calming effect rather than rage.

luna: Believers' mark is on their faces from prostration (سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ مِنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ); this connects the section's bodily sign to a visible trace of worship. | terra: Those seeking Allah's فضل and رضوان bear a mark on their faces from prostration. It is the section's strongest meeting of favorable pursuit, face, and worship.
terra: Allah makes faith beloved and disbelief hateful, then calls the resulting people rightly guided. Together with 49:8's فضل and نعمة, it defines favor as an oriented heart.
terra: Faith's lovers are the rightly guided in 49:7, and this ayah calls that state a فضل and نعمة from Allah. It makes guidance itself a bestowed favor.
luna: A person has only what he strives for; this supplies the effort side of 88:9's “pleased with her striving.”
luna: The striving will be seen; this explains how effort becomes relevant to the satisfied judgment in 88:9.
luna: The person will then be repaid in full; this completes the effort-and-outcome sequence related to 88:9.
terra: A screaming wind is sent upon 'Ad on a day of persistent misfortune. This is a concentrated scene of an adverse day arriving over a people.
terra: They are dragged on their faces into Fire. This physical abasement develops the section's lowly counterpart to the favored face.
luna: The sky becomes rose-red when split (وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ); the link to the section's B005 gloss for غضب as deep red is only a color parallel, not an anger scene.
terra: Criminals are recognized by their marks before seizure. The link is limited to the section's concern that final judgment becomes legible on a person rather than remaining hidden.
luna: The passage names the companions of the right as one group at the event; it is a specific parallel to the section's final division into communities.
luna: The next group is the companions of the left; the right/left pairing supplies a distinct two-group formulation, though the same chapter also names a third group.
luna: The chapter asks about the companions of the right and describes their garden's shade and fruit; this gives the favorable group's embodied outcome.
luna: The chapter asks about the companions of the left before describing their scorching wind and boiling water; this gives the contrasting group's adverse outcome.
luna: Believing men and women have light running before them and on their right on the Day; the image gives a visible sign of the favored group.
luna: A wall separates the believers from hypocrites, with mercy inside and punishment outside; this gives a sharp boundary between two groups on the Day, complementing 57:12's light.

luna: The verse contrasts hearts humbled at God's reminder with hearts that later harden; it offers an inward counterpart to the section's outward contrast between a softened and an anger-marked face.
terra: Some sought Allah's رضوان through monasticism but did not observe it as required. It is a boundary case where intending rıza needs faithful completion.

luna: The faithful are described as God's party, whom He supports and with whom He is pleased; this specifies a community on the accepted side of the section's division. | terra: Allah's party are those with faith written in their hearts; He is pleased with them and they with Him. It defines a community by the reciprocal rıza opposite the wrath-marked groups.
terra: The emigrants seek Allah's فضل and رضوان while supporting Allah and His Messenger. It shows rıza pursued through a concrete communal allegiance.

luna: The believers are told not to ally with a people God has angered, who have despaired of the Hereafter; it links the same anger-group to its lost expectation of the final day. | terra: Believers are told not to ally themselves with a people Allah is angry with. It treats divine غضب as a boundary that defines a group, as in 1:7.
terra: Eyes are lowered and humiliation covers them; they had been called to prostrate while sound. It reverses the willing prostration of the favored into a marked shame.
terra: A نعمة from Jonah's Lord reaches him so that he is not cast out blameworthy (مذموم). The verse explicitly sets favor against blame, the opposition developed for حمد in the section.
terra: The destructive wind is imposed on 'Ad for seven nights and eight days. It gives temporal extension to the section's days that bear a punitive descent.
terra: They emerge from graves with lowered eyes while humiliation covers them. It repeats the adverse face at the Day they were promised.

luna: Some faces on that day are radiant and looking toward their Lord; this is another explicit scene of a favorable face at judgment. | terra: Some faces on that Day are radiant. It is the broad eschatological counterpart to the section's favored face.

luna: The radiant faces of 75:22 look toward their Lord (إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ); it makes their appearance a stance of hopeful encounter, alongside the section's رضا. | terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord. The ayah completes 75:22's favorable orientation rather than merely naming brightness.

luna: Other faces that day are gloomy (بَاسِرَةٌ); the verse gives the opposite expression to the radiant faces in 75:22. | terra: Other faces on that Day are grim. It establishes the direct facial opposite within the same judgment scene.

luna: The gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity (تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ); it explains the fearful meaning of the expression in 75:24. | terra: Those grim faces expect a crushing calamity. It supplies the adverse fate that makes their facial state more than an expression.
terra: Those who feed others say they seek neither recompense nor thanks from them. This gives 76:10–11's feared grim day and granted radiance an ethic that refuses human praise as payment.
terra: The righteous fear a Day described as frowning and severe (عبوسا قمطريرا). It supplies the grim facial vocabulary immediately before 76:11's radiance and joy.

luna: God protects the righteous from that day's evil and meets them with radiance and joy (نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا); it joins deliverance to a visible, eased face. | terra: Allah protects them from the evil of that Day and gives them radiance and joy. It makes a day of danger end in the bright, eased face opposed to wrath.
luna: The righteous are told their striving has been appreciated (وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَشْكُورًا); this makes explicit why the satisfied effort in 88:9 belongs to a rewarded group.
terra: On the shaking Day, eyes are lowered. Its direct eye-state belongs with the section's account of emotion and judgment leaving signs around the eye.
terra: He frowned (عَبَسَ) and turned away. The section's dictionary gloss of غضوب as frowning finds a direct Quranic facial action, even though the root differs.

luna: Some faces that day are radiant (مُسْفِرَةٌ), beginning the paired facial scene the section uses for the two groups. | terra: Some faces on that Day are bright and shining. This is one of the section's cited favorable facial scenes.

luna: Those radiant faces laugh and rejoice (ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ); the verse specifies the expression of the favored side of the facial contrast. | terra: The shining faces are laughing and rejoicing, completing the soft and settled side of the section's contrast.

luna: Other faces that day have dust upon them (عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ); the “upon” construction closely matches the section's attention to what settles on a face. | terra: Other faces have dust upon them. The section explicitly reads this "upon them" as a facial counterpart to 1:7's عَلَيْهِم.

luna: A darkening covers those faces (تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ); this completes the image of a mark laid over the face, opposite the radiance in 80:38–39. | terra: Darkness covers those dust-marked faces. It completes the section's image of an adverse thing descending over the face.

luna: The chapter identifies the faces covered with dust and darkness in 80:40–41 as those of disbelievers and evildoers; it names the group represented by that adverse facial sign. | terra: The dust-darkened faces in 80:40–41 are identified as those of the disbelieving wicked. This ayah supplies the moral identity of that adverse facial scene.
luna: The verse names the Day of Judgment (يَوْمَ الدِّينِ) again; its question about what that day is makes the section's yawm word and accountability sense explicit.
luna: On that day no soul can do anything for another, and command belongs to God; this specifies the judgment-day boundary named in 82:18.

luna: The righteous' faces display “the radiance of bliss” (نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ); the verse directly extends the section's claim that favor leaves a recognizable mark on the face. | terra: The radiance of نعيم is recognized in their faces. It is the closest Quranic realization of the section's softened, blessed face.
terra: When the Quran is recited to them, they do not prostrate. It is the direct reversal of 19:58 and 17:107–109, where reception of the signs brings faces to the ground.

luna: “Faces that day” are described as humbled (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ); the verse supplies one side of the paired faces the section sets against نعمة. | terra: Other faces on that Day are humbled. It begins the adverse facial half that the section contrasts with the softened face.
terra: The humbled faces are laboring and weary. Its own contribution contrasts exhausted labor with 88:9's face satisfied with its effort.
terra: The laboring, humbled face enters a burning Fire. It supplies the immediate adverse destination for 88:2–3.

luna: The opposite faces on that day are called blissful/softened (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ), from the same ن ع م root as the section's أَنْعَمْتَ; it makes the root's bodily sense visible. | terra: Some faces on that Day are ناعمة, from the same ن ع م root as the section's أَنْعَمْتَ. It gives favor a literal facial condition.

luna: The blissful face is pleased with its striving (لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ); this connects the section's favor-and-pleasure contrast to the person's own work. | terra: That نعمة-marked face is satisfied with its effort (راضية). The ayah makes the favorable face and rıza explicit companions.
luna: The passage asks what God did to Aad, one of the peoples explicitly named in the section's gloss of “the days of Allah.”
luna: The same passage names Thamud and their rock-cut homes, the second people specifically named in that punishment gloss.
luna: Pharaoh is named next among the peoples who transgressed; this adds another historical example to the section's “and others” under the days of punishment.
luna: God pours a scourge of punishment upon those peoples (سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ); this is a particularly close image of judgment descending on a group.
luna: The passage closes by saying the Lord is watchful; it completes the punishment scene by grounding it in divine oversight.
luna: When provision is expanded, a person says his Lord has honored him; this gives a specific case of reading outward provision as favor.
luna: When provision is restricted, the person says his Lord has humiliated him; paired with 89:15, it exposes a mistaken equation between material state and divine standing.
luna: The answer begins “No!” and reproaches them for not honoring the orphan; this marks a boundary against treating abundance or deprivation alone as proof of approval or anger.

luna: The tranquil soul is addressed at the end of its course; the next verses say it returns pleased and pleasing, a direct inner counterpart to the section's softened, satisfied face. | terra: The soul addressed in 89:28 is first called tranquil. Its calmness is the inward inverse of the section's anger before the reciprocal rıza is named.

luna: The soul returns to its Lord “pleased and pleasing” (رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً); the paired رضا terms give the positive pole of the section's غضب/رضا opposition. | terra: The tranquil soul is commanded to return to its Lord راضية مرضية, a final reciprocal rıza that reverses the section's falling wrath.
luna: The pleased soul is invited among God's servants; the verse supplies the companionship side of the favored path.
luna: The same soul is invited into the Garden, completing the return and acceptance that contrast with falling under anger.
terra: The charitable seeker of the Most High's face will soon be satisfied. It gives rıza as the outcome of an enacted favorable pursuit.
terra: The Lord will give to the addressee and he will be satisfied (فترضى). The ayah makes divine giving culminate in rıza.
terra: Allah finds the addressee an orphan and gives shelter. It is a concrete prior gift in the sequence whose later result is satisfaction in 93:5.

luna: God says He found the Prophet wandering and guided him (ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ); this is a compact reversal from lost direction to bestowed guidance. | terra: The wording says Allah found the addressee ضالًّا and guided him. Whatever its exegetical scope, its own verbal pairing directly meets the section's guidance-versus-ضلّين concern.

luna: God says He found the Prophet needy and enriched him; it pairs provision with the guidance in 93:7, matching the section's joined favor-and-path imagery. | terra: Allah finds the addressee in need and makes him self-sufficient. It gives the gift-side of the section a concrete reversal of lack.
terra: The command to proclaim the Lord's نعمة makes favor answerable in speech, linking the section's ni'ma to its opening language of praise.
luna: The disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists are named as the worst of creation and assigned the Fire; this is one side of the paired final groups.
luna: Believers who do good are named as the best of creation; this sets the favored community against the group in 98:6.

luna: Their reward is gardens, and God is pleased with them while they are pleased with Him; this directly completes the two-group contrast with the section's positive رضا pole. | terra: The Garden's people receive the formula "Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him," giving the favorable community its final mutual rıza.

luna: People will be questioned that day about “the bliss” (النَّعِيمِ); the verse directly joins the section's ن ع م family to its yawm/day theme. | terra: On that Day people will be questioned about نعيم. It turns the section's favorable gift into an accountable possession within its yawm horizon.
